claim: llm-d is officially described by its own contributors (Google, IBM Research) as an 'open-source, k8s-native, pluggable inference stack', explicitly framing Kubernetes-nativity as a core design tenet alongside accelerator-agnosticism.
stance_target: feasibility of swapping non-k8s backends into llm-d's router without touching core assumptions
scope_conditions: PyTorch Conference talk, llm-d project representatives
quoted_support: Open-source, k8s-native, pluggable inference stack. Accelerator agnostic. Streamlined well-lit paths.

claim: The P/D inference scheduler's disaggregation decision is gated by a threshold on the percentage of new (uncached) tokens to prefill; below threshold no disaggregation occurs, above it the scheduler runs separate D-picking and P-picking plugin sets (cache utilization/queue depth for D; prefix cache hit/queue depth for P).
stance_target: scheduler decision mechanics for P/D dispatch
quoted_support: % new tokens to prefill > threshold? ... Pick D (configurable plugins): kv cache utilization, queue depth. Pick P (configurable plugins): Prefix cache hit, Queue depth.

claim: The reference 'P/D over RDMA' well-lit path benchmark uses 8xH200 GPUs with InfiniBand or RoCE RDMA, serving Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8 with 4 TP=1 prefill workers and 1 TP=4 decode worker.
quoted_support: P/D over RDMA: 8xH200 GPUs, InfiniBand OR RoCE RDMA, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8, 4 TP=1 Prefill Workers, 1 TP=4 Decode Worker

claim: The 'wide-EP with P/D' benchmark uses 32xH200 GPUs with InfiniBand or RoCE RDMA to serve DeepSeek-R1-0528 with 1 DP=16 prefill worker and 1 DP=16 decode worker.
stance_target: concrete reference hardware/topology for wide expert-parallel P/D
quoted_support: Wide-ep (expert parallelism) with P/D: 32xH200 GPUs, InfiniBand OR RoCE RDMA, DeepSeek-R1-0528, 1 DP=16 Prefill worker, 1 DP=16 decode workers

claim: llm-d project maintainers have identified 'decode-first PD' as unshipped future work: because the router lacks visibility into remote KV-cache storage, they propose opportunistically routing to a decoder first and only invoking P/D if the decoder itself reports low cache hit (computed locally via vLLM's KVConnector).
stance_target: known gap in current router cache-awareness, roadmap item
scope_conditions: presented as future work, not yet implemented as of this talk
quoted_support: Router doesn't have info about cache in remote storage -> let vLLM calculate local+remote cache hit (via KVConnector). Router opportunistically pick decoder with potentially high cache hit to avoid P/D. Decoder returns "low cache hit" and router will then pick P/D.

claim: llm-d's current gateway picks both P and D endpoints at request-arrival time, which can use stale load metrics since the request only lands on the decode worker later; 'deferred decoder picking' (choosing D after prefill completes) is proposed as future work to use freshest load data.
stance_target: limitation in current scheduling timing, roadmap item
quoted_support: Currently gateway picks P and D at request arrival time. However the request lands on D at a later time -> load can be stale. Idea: Pick D after prefill is done, with freshest load metrics.

claim: llm-d best practice guidance recommends exploring P/D disaggregation only for large models (Llama-70B+, not Llama-8B), longer input sequence lengths (e.g. 10k ISL | 1k OSL vs 200|200), and sparse MoE architectures with wide-EP opportunities, and to tune heterogeneous parallelism and P:D replica ratios rather than applying P/D uniformly.
stance_target: P/D disaggregation is a workload-specific optimization, not universal
quoted_support: P/D disaggregation is not a target for all workloads. We suggest exploring P/D disaggregation for workloads with: Large models (e.g. Llama-70B+, not Llama-8B), Longer input sequence lengths (e.g 10k ISL | 1k OSL, not 200 ISL | 200 OSL), Sparse MoE architectures with opportunities for wide-EP
